newsitem.title: ITALY: ATHLETICS-KOMEN LEADS RACE FOR MEN'S OVERALL GRAND PRIX TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-KOMEN LEADS RACE FOR MEN'S OVERALL GRAND PRIX TITLE.

text.p: Daniel Komen, who smashed Noureddine Morceli's world 3,000 metres record last Sunday, leads the race for the men's overall title at Saturday's grand prix final.
The 20-year-old Kenyan goes to Milan four points ahead of Morceli, former world champion hurdler Samuel Matete and world triple jump recordholder Jonathan Edwards.

American 100 metres champion Dennis Mitchell and Olympic 400 metres hurdles champion Derrick Adkins are also in contention for the overall prize which could be worth as much as $350,000 to the eventual winner.
The prize money consists of $200,000 for winning the overall title, $50,000 for winning an individual event and $100,000 for setting a world record.
Komen is in such blistering form that he could well set a second world record inside a week.
At the Zurich grand prix on August 14 he just missed out on breaking Haile Gebreselassie's 5,000 metres world record of 12:44.39 when he clocked 12:45.09, the second fastest time in history.
Last Sunday in Rieti he destroyed Morceli's 3,000 record and if he sets another world record on Saturday in the 5,000 he would gain 45 grand prix points and ensure first place.
Morceli, though, has also been in good form recently and could secure the overall title he last won in 1994, with a world record victory in the 1,500 metres.

The top four chasing the women's title are American sprinter Gwen Torrence and Swedish Olympic 100 metres hurdles champion Ludmilla Engquist, both on 66 points, and Jamaican sprinters Michelle Freeman (64 points) and Merlene Ottey (63 points), the overall grand prix winner in 1987 and 1990.

Russian Svetlana Masterkova, who won the 800-1500 double in the Atlanta Olympics and set world records over 1,000 metres and mile in Brussels and Zurich last month. Although she is out of contention for the overall prize she should end her season with victory in the 1,500 metres.
Twelve world records have been set at the historic Arena stadium, now restored after years of neglect. The last was Ed Moses's 400 metres hurdles record of 47.13 seconds in 1980.
